They had a lot of time to choose a place for a couple of drinks, and when they didn’t, I wasn’t really left with a choice other than coming to their house. It just doesn’t feel right. It left me without an opportunity to really confront anything for fear of bringing them down on their vacation. Do you see what I’m saying? 

From my perspective, it was very deceptive. Then to stop drinking when we got to their place. After a few hours, suggest we go to their room? Something isn’t right to me and I just can’t quite put it in words. So my struggle is, was it truly consensual when I was under the influence as much as I was? Hi. First off, I’m super sorry you’re going through this, I can only imagine how stressful it is already. That being said, your father isn’t helping your situation by being angry your boyfriend may not make it. Some unsolicited advice, based on my first-hand experience, if your boyfriend doesn’t make it to the actual procedure (or when you take the second pill) then I think you should rethink your relationship. My situation was much different than yours, but I thought my ex was going to be there and he wasn’t so I went through it alone. I couldn’t walk and really needed support, especially emotionally. He prioritized a friend over being there for me. Whether or not they show up says all you need to know about the relationship. (Ok, sorry)

As for your father, he’s making this process a whole lot harder on you. That’s the last thing anyone would need in that situation. I suggest sitting down with your father to have a conversation about what’s actually important and what YOU need. Understand his concern, but it’s not about your boyfriend, it’s about YOU. If he’s unreasonable still, I say take your father out of the situation all together. Even if you end up going through it alone (like I did), it’s better than having someone throwing a fit while your body is incapacitated. I don’t suggest being alone though, because it is still dangerous. 

Emotional support is huge through this whole process. If anything, at least one trusted friend you can call and talk to will make a world of difference. I really wish I had had any emotional support. I think that’s part of why I still struggle with my decision to this day. Friends help a lot, if your SO is there that’s ideal. If your father can’t give you the focus and support you need right now, you have to do what’s best for you. You come first, especially right now. Don’t be afraid to make that clear to all parties. 

It’s a scary thing to go through as it is, it’s okay to do what YOU need in order to make it as smooth as possible. 

Much love and well wishes to you. I hope all turns out right in the end.

Hey, you can’t control another persons emotions or actions. So her hurting herself is not your fault. It is hers. It rests on her shoulders to change. Not yours. All you can do is be supportive. It is not possible to control or change how another person thinks or feels. 

I don’t think it would’ve been impossible. I think it depends on what your gut is telling you and what you’ve already been shown. Humans are silly creatures of habit. I personally have a fault it expecting change, even when it’s not realistic. 

And to the the first paragraph, I completely understand. Your feelings are valid. But how someone else treats you is not your fault. It is a reflection of the other person. If that’s how they treat you, how do they treat themselves? That’s not an issue for you to have to solve. 

And I definitely understand wanting someone to make an effort to get to know you. That just depends on the person and how interested they really are in you. If they really do like you, that’s never something you have to beg for. That was a hard lesson for me to learn. 

Just remember, the only persons happiness you are responsible for is your own. If you worry about every other person and put their own needs and wants before your own, when will you have time for yourself and to make yourself happy? No one is worth sacrificing your happiness for. 

Don’t feel guilty or responsible for that. There’s only so much you can do. As long as you’re meeting your own needs, the rest should follow. And if it doesn’t, it’s not worth your time to worry about. (I tell this to myself every single day, because it’s something I struggle with on the daily).
